feedback_request.integration_feedback: Report max_error on oval, s-bend and slalom compared with 0.060, 0.062 and 0.062 at 0.8 kg. Say whether line_loss_events stayed at 0. Say whether the robot shows a faster or more responsive turn at 0.6 kg, and whether steering_oscillation changed (it was 0.074 on oval, 0.067 on s-bend and 0.064 on slalom at 0.8 kg). Say whether any controller gain needed a change for the lighter body, such as kp or kd.

intent: Single-lever test of mass: iteration 4's geometry with mass reduced from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. Sensor span ±0.05, y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12 m and wheel_radius 0.035 m are unchanged, so the result isolates mass. Expected: max_error on oval and s-bend drops below about 0.058 with line_loss_events at 0. If it does not move, the floor is not a mass effect.
learning: Iterations 0 to 4 show that max_error sits at 0.0601 to 0.0621 across span (±0.04 to ±0.06), footprint, lookahead, wheel_track (0.10 to 0.12) and wheel_radius (0.03 to 0.035). Line losses are fixed by a span of ±0.05 or wider. Slalom progress was 0.110 at ±0.04 (with line losses) and 0.035 at ±0.05 and ±0.06 (without). So the remaining levers are mass, sensor footprint and a larger radius. Mass is tested now.
rationale: Iteration 4 (±0.05 span, wheel_radius 0.035, wheel_track 0.12) kept line losses at 0 and moved max_error only slightly: oval 0.0601 (from 0.0614), s-bend 0.062 and slalom 0.0621 (no change). Max_error is still pinned near 0.061 on every track in every design, so the wheel_radius lever did not move the floor. Span, footprint, lookahead and wheel_track have also been ruled out (iterations 0 to 4). The Integrator's rule for this case is to test mass 0.6 kg next. I keep the ±0.05 span, which gave no line losses, and the 0.035 radius, which did not hurt. I change only mass, from 0.8 to 0.6 kg, so any shift in the floor can be attributed to mass. Lower mass reduces yaw inertia, which may let the robot correct a steady drift faster. Expected result: if max_error on oval and s-bend falls below about 0.058 with line_loss_events still 0, mass is a real lever and I will tune it next. If it stays at about 0.060 to 0.062, the floor is not a body-geometry effect, and I will move to sensor_size or a larger wheel_radius (0.04). Slalom progress is still at 0.035 and is not the focus of this test.
